title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We present a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes, yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts (per‑file SHA‑256 manifest) and show—using archived traces and hashes—why the preregistered shared‑candidate design produced a degenerate but correct confirmatory outcome. We then document artifact‑grounded, runnable remedies (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory designs, validator diversification, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while permitting informative inference about independent LLM generative reliability. The immutable initial master prompt is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Automating NetOps tasks by translating high‑level intent into device configurations promises operator productivity gains but raises correctness and safety concerns: generated commands must preserve reachability, respect access control invariants, and obey transient safety constraints during multi‑step changes. Deterministic validators that compute semantic effects of configurations (reachability, ACL enforcement, transient invariants) are widely used to reduce deployment risk prior to device push (see Batfish lessons and related verifier literature). Our study asks a focused, preregistered question: under a frozen paired design, does a single‑pass LLM generator produce verifier‑passing configurations less often than a deterministic template baseline? We preregistered the experimental plan (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) and archived every execution artifact to permit exact reproduction and audit (execution/execution_manifest.json contains the exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 manifest).
sections.related_work: Prior NetOps LLM work emphasizes generate–validate–repair loops and the necessity of verifier grounding: several recent studies evaluate intent→configuration pipelines with both language metrics and semantic validators but often omit preregistered estimands or full artifact publication. Other efforts produce benchmarks for intent translation and configuration synthesis but differ in task heterogeneity and validator scope. Unlike evaluations that sample independent generations per condition, our preregistered confirmatory design used a shared_initial_candidate semantics (a single canonical candidate per task reused across conditions) to isolate validator treatment differences; as we show, this isolates a different question than independent generative reliability. Representative prior sources that informed our positioning are included in the artifact bundle and verified citation list (for example: https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866; https://doi.org/10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407; https://doi.org/10.1002/nem.70029).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen analysis plan. The full preregistration CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 (SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) specified: N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS), paired confirmatory analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate". The plan froze seeds, inclusion/exclusion rules, the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation), retry policy (up to two automatic retries for infrastructure failures), and the exact adapter family (hosted_netops_gvr_v1). These frozen fields, and the execution contract (maximum_model_calls = 240, model_names = ["gpt‑5‑mini"]) are archived in execution/execution_manifest.json; execution began at 2026‑08‑27T14:49:02.808900+00:00 and completed at 2026‑08‑27T15:04:49.334056+00:00, with model_calls_used = 120 and completed_episode_count = 240.
sections.results: Confirmatory quantitative outcome (artifact‑grounded). All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed without infrastructure failures (complete_pair_count = 120). The archived per‑condition counts are baseline_success_count = 120/120 and guarded_success_count = 120/120 (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f...). The paired contingency table is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Under the preregistered paired estimator the mean guarded − baseline = 0.00; the 95% bootstrap percentile CI using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.00,0.00], and the exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All numerical outputs and the analysis log are archived under analysis/ (paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...).
sections.discussion: Diagnosis from archived traces. The archive shows that, for many pairs, the shared_initial canonical candidate file used by both conditions is byte‑identical across baseline, guarded, and shared initial artifacts (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e..., execution/responses/task-000003‑shared‑initial.txt SHA‑256 f7f4db24...). Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) enforces per‑task required_sequence and workflow_policies (e.g., make‑before‑break, must_be_down_for_fields) present in the templated tasks; when an identical candidate satisfies those constraints both conditions necessarily receive identical pass judgments. Thus the confirmatory paired test assessed validator parity across conditions for identical artifacts—not independent generative reliability under stochastic sampling.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published a complete artifact bundle enabling byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, both the deterministic template baseline and the recorded LLM pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini) validated on all confirmatory episodes (both 120/120). Archived artifacts show identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints produced the degenerate paired outcome; consequently the confirmatory paired result is arithmetically correct but not informative about independent LLM generative reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded procedural remedies (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory execution, validator diversification, and expanded task heterogeneity) and we publish the exact files and hashes necessary to reexecute these alternate confirmatory tests using the same deterministic harness. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
